headline: Learned models link histology and spatial transcriptomics to predict expression and niches
label: Learned Representations For Spatial Transcriptomics
summary: Multimodal and graph-based learned encoders now recover gene expression, cell states and tissue domains from histology and spot-level data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned latent representations that recover structure from spatial transcriptomics and histology. Several items predict spot-level expression from H&E: HESpotEx, a dual-stream graph attention autoencoder, covers up to 5,457 genes, and an EfficientNet-B0 single-patch baseline addresses liver and breast cancer Visium data. STARS applies a Vision Transformer with contrastive learning to reconstruct single-cell expression across Visium and Visium HD, while HAST applies heterogeneity-driven graph learning at subcellular resolution and HESTIA integrates histology with high-resolution data for spatial domain identification. TMEformer and TRINUS extend learned models to in silico perturbation and to separating lineage from niche pressure. Prostate-TriMod adds a tri-modal resource linking virtual H&E, immune and epithelial maps and clinical outcomes. The set is heterogeneous: Bayesian mSGR regression and mass spectrometry imaging manifold learning pursue related goals through different formulations.
